root.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Main Line
root.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nd2 dxe4 4. Nxe4

overview: After 3.Nc3 or 3.Nd2 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Black develops with ...Bf5 (Classical) or ...Nf6 (5.Nxf6+ exf6 or ...Nd7 lines). Black gets a healthy structure and a free light-squared bishop and aims for ...e6 and ...c5. White has a lead in space and development and tries for Qf3 and Bd3 with kingside play, but Black's position is very hard to break down.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Ng3, Nf3 and Bd3 against the bishop; sometimes h4-h5 to harass Bf5-g6
Use the space and any kingside majority; in the 5.Nxf6+ line, play for Bc4 and Ne2

black_ideas.idea: Develop the bishop outside the chain, then ...e6, ...Nd7 and ...Ngf6
Break with ...c5 once developed, aiming for a sound middlegame

typical_structures.structure: White d4 against Black c6/e6 with the bishop outside, asymmetric centre

character.notes: The Classical Caro-Kann is Solid by anchor: few weaknesses and slow play.

gambit.notes: Pawn on e4 is taken, none given.

structure.notes: d4 against c6/e6, half-open lines, semi-open.

character.reason: Black's structure is hard to break down in the Classical Caro-Kann.

structure.reason: Asymmetric centre with White d4 against c6/e6.

approach.reason: A main-line defence at all levels.
